data.title: Archer Aviation's Warrants Expire September 16. What Does It Mean for ACHR Stock?
data.description:
Archer Aviation Inc. (ACHR) filed an 8-K confirming that the New York Stock Exchange has halted trading in its public warrants, ACHR WS, ahead of their September 16 expiration. The move does not affect Archer's common stock, which continues to trade normally on the NYSE under the ACHR ticker.

The warrants allow holders to buy one share of Archer Class A common stock at an exercise price of $11.50. They will expire at 5:00 p.m. ET on September 16, 2026, and any warrants left unexercised at that point will become void.

The NYSE halted trading in ACHR WS on September 1 and plans to suspend the warrants before the market opens on September 15.

data.title: Broadcom (AVGO) Hit With Street-Low Target Despite Strong Quarter – Here's Why
data.description:
Broadcom (AVGO) has received a new Street-low price target even after the semiconductor company posted another strong quarter. Despite upbeat results, near‑term revenue guidance did not fully meet the high bar investors had set, which weighed on the stock. Top-rated DA Davidson analyst Gil Luria cut his price target to $350 from $400, while keeping a Hold rating. The new target implies 2.2% downside risk from the current level.

The analyst also raised concerns that the company leans heavily on big AI customers and that long‑term demand depends on tight land, power, and data center buildout needs. Luria now values Broadcom at 19× his updated FY27 EPS estimate.

Strong Quarter, but Guidance Fell Short of High Hopes

Broadcom reported Q3 revenue of $29.6 billion, up 85% year over year and slightly above estimates. Its semiconductor unit grew 127% to $20.8 billion, now making up 70% of total revenue. The company said shipments of its custom AI chips, called XPUs, rose 3.5× from last year and now account for 73% of its AI revenue.

The company gave long‑term AI revenue guidance through 2028 to show the strength of its pipeline. The company expects AI chip revenue to double in 2027 to $115 billion, then rise again in 2028 to $230 billion, far above Wall Street's 2028 expectations.

AVGO also shared its delivery plans for its biggest AI customers, saying it will ship 1 GW to Anthropic in 2026, 5 GW in 2027, and 10 GW in 2028. For OpenAI, the company expects to deliver 1.3 GW in 2027 and 5 GW in 2028.

Management expects the cost per gigawatt to stay steady at $20 billion to $30 billion, noting that more powerful chips need fewer units to hit 1 GW.

Broadcom expects a slight margin dip next quarter due to higher memory costs inside its chips. Q4 gross margin is expected to be 73%, down from 75%.

data.description:
The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) and the Nasdaq 100 ETF (QQQ) closed with mixed performance on Friday. The S&P 500 ETF finished with a 0.38% loss, while the Nasdaq 100 ETF rose 0.19%.

News That Moved the Stock Market Today

  • The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) announced that nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 in August, shattering expectations of 55,000. In addition, the unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%.
  • Following the data, the odds of a 25-basis-point hike at the September 16 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting rallied to 58.4% from 49.4% a day ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool. With jobs growth remaining strong, the Fed has more flexibility to concentrate on inflation, which has remained above the central bank's 2% target for over 65 months.
  • Furthermore, President Trump threatened to end trade with all countries the U.S. has a deficit with unless the Fed cuts rates. "LOWER THE RATE OR I'LL STOP TRADING WITH COUNTRIES WITH WHICH WE HAVE A DEFICIT," he said in a Truth Social post.
  • In a separate post, he said the "fear of inflation" is holding back economic growth and pressuring the stock market.
  • The Fed will receive two key inflation datapoints next week with the Producer Price Index (PPI) and Consumer Price Index (CPI).
  • Tesla (TSLA) closed in the red after its Cybercab debut failed to resonate with investors. "But Tesla didn't provide specific numbers or a launch timeline," said Wells Fargo analyst Colin Langan.
  • Lululemon (LULU) plummeted after issuing full-year sales guidance of $10.35-$10.5 billion, down from its prior estimate of $11-$11.5 billion. In addition, its same-store sales fell 9% year-over-year in the second quarter.
  • PayPal (PYPL) sank after Axios reported that the payment processor had halted plans to sell its $1 billion venture portfolio. Earlier this week, Betaville said PayPal had attracted takeover interest from an undisclosed party.
  • Netflix (NFLX) trended lower after the company announced plans to raise subscription prices in the United Kingdom.

data.title: IBM and Microsoft Back U.S. Quantum Bill as House Panel Advances the American Quantum Competitiveness Act
data.description:
A new quantum computing bill cleared a House subcommittee, marking a major push to protect key supply chains. Representative Nick Langworthy introduced the American Quantum Competitiveness Act to build a national tech plan. The bill has drawn strong support from major tech leaders, including IBM (IBM), Microsoft (MSFT), and Google (GOOGL).

As a direct result of this industry backing, the Quantum Industry Coalition is rallying to pass the measure. The group noted that the law will help create a unified national strategy to boost research and commercial growth.

The Bill Centralizes Quantum Policy Power

Under current rules, quantum policy duties are spread out across several federal groups without a single leader. Moving to fix that problem, the new bill elevates the Commerce Secretary to serve as chief advisor to the president on quantum policy and commercial growth.

Building on that change, the Energy Department currently plays a major role through its national labs. Other agencies like the Department of Defense and National Science Foundation also fund projects, while standards groups work on quantum-safe network rules.

Commerce Department Will Track Quantum Parts Made Abroad

To keep supply lines safe, the Commerce Department will track quantum parts made outside the country. Following that tracking work, officials will take active steps to cut down reliance on foreign supply chains.

Beyond basic computing, the bill covers connected tools like sensors and advanced communication systems. Pure computing firms like IonQ (IONQ) and Infleqtion (INFQ) have already grown into these new areas to win federal contracts.

This legislative push follows a $2 billion Commerce Department package and June executive orders aimed at building local production. While the text does not name China directly, the subtext points to growing competition with Beijing's tech goals.

China highlighted quantum science in its recent cyber priority updates, pushing local firms to pursue major breakthroughs. Since quantum systems can break current data codes and aid defense networks, U.S. lawmakers want to ensure breakthroughs turn into American products and jobs.

Which Quantum Computing Stocks Are a Buy?

Among pure-play firms, IonQ trades near $39.52 with a Strong Buy rating and a $69.44 price target, pointing to 75% upside. Smaller pure-play names like D-Wave Quantum (QBTS) and Quantum Computing Inc. (QUBT) show targets above 100% upside. Major tech firms like Alphabet (GOOGL) carry a perfect 10 Smart Score, while Nvidia (NVDA) and Microsoft (MSFT) hold Strong Buy ratings as government contracts expand.

data.title: Ripple CEO Calls Out Central Bank's $11 Billion Gold Move as 'Too Slow' XRP Ledger Tests 3-Second Speed
data.description:
Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse pointed to an $11 billion gold move by the Dutch central bank as proof that traditional finance is "too slow." De Nederlandsche Bank sold 59 tonnes of gold in New York and bought the same amount back in London. Because of that structure, nearly 70% of the total gold move was just a paper trade, while only 27 tonnes actually flew across the ocean.

Building on that point, Garlinghouse contrasted those slow bank methods with digital assets. He noted that the crypto market grew from a $1.5 billion test into a $2.7 trillion asset class over the last ten years.

XRP Ledger Tests Show Fast Network Settlement

While gold moves rely on physical flights and paper trades, digital networks offer a much faster path. The Bank for International Settlements recently ran tests on the XRP Ledger, where the network linked official central bank data in three to five seconds, with check times taking just one to two seconds.

data.title: Zcash Price Surges Past $1,000 as Grayscale Forecasts Hypothetical $8,100 ZEC Price Target Using a Bitcoin Model
data.description: Zcash (ZEC-USD) broke the $1,000 price mark as a mix of new ETF buying and forced short seller sales pushed the coin past four figures for the first time in nearly ten years. Zcash price trades near $1,009, up roughly 28% over the past five days and nearly 100% over the past month. Grayscale researchers point out that Zcash uses a hard 21 million coin supply cap, making it similar to Bitcoin's fixed supply model. The firm noted a hypothetical picture where ZEC could hit $8,100 if it captured 10% of Bitcoin's market value.
